summary: @servicetitan/hammer-token preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: The package's `preinstall` script `setup.mjs` is heavily obfuscated (hex-named identifiers, control-flow flattening) and, on `npm install`, downloads a platform-specific Bun runtime archive from `github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases`, extracts it to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and uses that freshly-downloaded runtime to execute the sibling file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a 727 KB Bun-compiled artifact (`// @bun @bun-cjs`) with string-array rotation (`WV8StW`), a large numeric/string dictionary (`n7gIxM`), and control-flow flattening — its network endpoints and behavior are reconstructed at runtime from the char-code table and are not visible to Node-based inspection. The package's advertised purpose is a style-dictionary/design-tokens exporter (`main: build/web/index.js`, README describes styledictionary.com token tooling); running an alternate JS runtime at install time to invoke an opaque 700+KB blob has no relationship to that purpose. A separate file `src/utils/figma/get-token.js` also combines `child_process`, `http`, filesystem reads, and `process.env` reads with POST/fetch calls. The alternate-runtime-dropper pattern is designed to evade Node-based static analysis of the actual payload.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
